summary: Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (Karabchampa, 1990) and Harvard University (PhD, ~1997–2004 under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Thomas Burke, and Khenchen Trinley Paljor).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (Acharya), and Harvard University (PhD, 2004). He served as a visiting scholar at the University of Michigan and Numata Visiting Professor at McGill (2016).

Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar (1895–1963) was an Indian historian and Indologist. Educated at the University of Mumbai, he served as a faculty member at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from ~1939 to 1955.
Tré Khen Zur Lozang Wangchuk was a scholar who pursued his traditional studies under the 13th Dalai Lama, Trijang Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Tse-fu Kuan completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Oxford in 2004 under Richard Gombrich. He held a postdoctoral research post at National Cheng Kung University and was affiliated with Yuan Ze University in 2015.
Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche (1914–1983) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Geshe Lharampa degree at Ganden Monastery, where he also held a post.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang (1951–2018) worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Villages (B.Ed), and the University of Glasgow (1987), serving as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Villages and Instructor in Tibetan at Oxford (2001).

A Tibetology and history scholar, Tsering Shakya earned his BA, MPhil, and BA degrees at SOAS University of London. He was a research fellow at SOAS (1999–2002), taught at Oxford, and joined the University of British Columbia (~2007).

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche (1953–2020) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at the Young Lamas Home School, he served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and sat on the board of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Tsoknyi Rinpoche studied at Khampagar Monastery (~1979) and under several teachers, including Dilgo Khyentse and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi (1951–2021) was a linguist and Tibetologist. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University Bloomington (PhD under Christopher I. Beckwith), later serving as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1999–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo (1936–2019) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University (PhD, 1985), he taught at Rissho and served as President of Reiyukai (~1975–1996) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013), studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima is an Indology and history scholar who earned bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995) and the University of Tokyo (1997–2018).

Tsultrim Allione is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology practitioner and author. She earned a master's degree from Antioch University and studied under traditional teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Apho Rinpoche, and Namkhai Norbu.

Tsultrim Gyatso worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held positions as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

Tsultrim Kelsang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer and professor at Otani University (attested 1984–2002) and held a research post at Ryukoku University in 2015.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education. He held posts at Doshisha University and served as a professor at Kyoto University from ~1996 to 2007.
Tsutomu Hatai is an Indology scholar who served as the president of Ayurveda Kenkyukai, attested in 1987 after succeeding Hiroshi Maruyama.

Tsutomu Kubo (1883–1972) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University (1953). He taught at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University (1929–1946), and Toyo University (~1949–1954).
